identificationModule.officialTitle: Clinical Trial for the Safety and Efficacy of Sequential CD19 and CD22 CAR-T Therapy for Adult Patients With Newly Diagnosed Ph Chromosome Negative B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a prospective, single arm study. To evaluate the safety and efficacy of sequential CD19 and CD22 CAR-T cells in the treatment of adult newly diagnosed Ph chromosome negative B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The main endpoints were dose limiting toxicity (DLT) and incidence of adverse events (TEAEs).

primaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events assessed according to NCI-CTCAE v5.0 criteria
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline up to 28 days after CAR-T cells infusion

primaryOutcomes.description: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events \[Safety and Tolerability\]
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years after CAR-T cells infusion

secondaryOutcomes.description: Complete Remission Rate after CAR-T cell therapy
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: up to 28 days after CAR-T cells infusion

secondaryOutcomes.description: From the first infusion of CD19 CAR-T cells to death or the last visit
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years after CD19 CAR-T cells infusion

secondaryOutcomes.description: From the complete remission to the occurrence of any event, including death, relapse (any one occurs first), and the last visit
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years after CD19 CAR-T cells infusion

secondaryOutcomes.description: Assessment using European Organisation for the Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) scale \[For item1-28: max score: 112, min score: 28, higher scores mean a better outcome; for item 28-29: max score: 14, min score: 2, higher scores mean a worse outcome\] to measure Quality of life at Baseline, Month 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12
